verifiedProperties.decimalGuard: constructor requires IERC20Metadata(token_).decimals() == 6 -- deploy-time USDC guard, unchanged

newState.name: nudgeStreamer
newState.init: address(0) -- setter-only, deliberately NOT a constructor arg

criticalDistinction: THIS is the one of the four with NO donation-disable switch and NO try/catch. `batchMinter` cannot be zeroed (setBatchMinter requires non-zero, and the constructor requires non-zero). There is no `donationSplit`. Therefore any balance > 0 forces the streamer path, and an unwired/misregistered streamer REVERTS `dispatch` -- which is called from NFTMinterV2.mint (NFTMinterV2.sol:191), so the whole MINT bricks, not just the donation.

orderedOpsSequence: ALSO: batchMinter.setNudgeStreamer(nudgeStreamer) for the pot flush at batchMint step 3.5
wiringRequirements.deployToWireWindow: Between deployment and step 3, every mint through this dispatcher reverts "NudgeRatchet: nudgeStreamer unset" (given any non-zero balance). Previously the legacy safeTransfer path made this window impossible.
rearmingActions: setBatchMinter to an address with no registered (newMinter, _token) stream -> every dispatch reverts NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered
streamer owner un-registering / re-registering with duration 0 (reverts at registerStream, so not reachable)

externalEntryPoints.function: dispatch(address minter, uint256 amount, bytes extraData) [base, non-virtual]
stateChanges: none local; token allowance to streamer; token balance

dispatchCallGraph: require(bal >= amount, 'NudgeRatchet: insufficient balance for dispatch')
-- then base: hook.onDispatch(minter, amount, extraData)  [debt on `amount`, not `bal`]
removedBehaviour: IERC20(_token).safeTransfer(batchMinter, bal) -- REMOVED, no fallback retained.

preconditionsAndInvariants.balGuard: if (bal > 0) prevents NudgeStreamer__ZeroAmount. LOAD-BEARING: without it a zero-balance dispatch would revert and brick the mint. Note bal >= amount is already required, so bal == 0 implies amount == 0.
preconditionsAndInvariants.hookTypeGuard: hookTypeId() must match EXPECTED_HOOK_TYPE_ID -- refuses to dispatch through a missing/wrong hook. Unchanged. Relevant to the standing 'unwired-hook zero-debt' drift-watch: on THIS contract a wrong hook is a loud revert, not a silent zero-debt.
preconditionsAndInvariants.overBackingInvariant: bal >= amount, and the full bal is handed to the streamer. Debt accrues on `amount`. Surplus is over-backing (protocol-favouring). PRESERVED under the streamer change in aggregate terms, but see value-flow: the surplus now arrives at the batchMinter over time rather than immediately.
preconditionsAndInvariants.noRescue: No rescueERC20 on this contract. Self-cleaning was the stated rationale (the sweep forwards stray USDC on the next dispatch). Under the mandatory-streamer design the self-cleaning property now depends on the streamer being correctly wired.

decimalAndScale.conversions: NONE -- bal is passed through verbatim to collectNudge. No new decimal surface.
decimalAndScale.streamerScale: PRECISION=1e18 cancels; native 6-dp units preserved. For a 1e6 (1 USDC) buffer, rewardPerSecond = 1e24/duration; only duration > 1e24 would truncate to zero, which is not a plausible configuration.
decimalAndScale.driftWatchStatus: M-03 decimal-under-mint class: CLEAN, no new conversion introduced.

valueFlow.afterStory046: minter -> ratchet -> NudgeStreamer buffer[(batchMinter, USDC)] -> batchMinter linearly over `duration`

whoHoldsTokens.successBranch: NudgeStreamer holds the donation; batchMinter receives only the amount accrued since the previous settle (which, when the previous settle was in the same block, is zero).
whoHoldsTokens.failureBranch: ENTIRE dispatch reverts -> the mint reverts -> the minter's transferFrom is rolled back -> no tokens move at all. Nothing is stranded on the ratchet, but user mints are unavailable.

valueFlow.strandOrDoublePay: No double-pay. Strand risk is the streamer-side one: value in buffer[(oldBatchMinter, USDC)] after a setBatchMinter re-point has no recovery path (NudgeStreamer has no rescue, and only the OLD batchMinter can pullPendingStream).
valueFlow.timingShift: The batchMint 'donate forward' incentive is preserved and slightly strengthened: the streamer flush at batchMint step 3.5 and the in-loop collectNudge share a timestamp, so a batch cannot settle its own donations back to itself.

externalCalls.notes: NOT wrapped in try/catch. A revert here reverts the mint.

trustAssumptions: The streamer owner registers (batchMinter, USDC) before setNudgeStreamer / setBatchMinter.
Owner sequences the four wiring steps correctly; the contract enforces none of the cross-contract preconditions.

localObservations.note: Mandatory streamer with NO disable switch and NO try/catch. `nudgeStreamer == 0`, an unregistered (batchMinter, USDC) pair, or ANY revert inside collectNudge (including the streamer's outbound _settle transfer to batchMinter, e.g. a USDC blacklist on the batchMinter) reverts the whole mint via NFTMinterV2:191. This is a strictly wider mint-brick surface than the removed safeTransfer. The NatSpec pre-declares it 'NOT an audit finding'; recorded here as a fact for interaction/severity analysis to weigh, not adjudicated.
forceApprove(streamer, bal) is never reset to zero. Safe only while collectNudge pulls the full `bal`.

Of the four donors this is the only one where the streamer requirement is unconditional. BalancerPoolerV2 catches it; Uniboost and PromotionUniV2_Eth scope it to a disable-able donation branch. Cross-check that this asymmetry is intended.

The NatSpec still describes the sweep as making rescueERC20 unnecessary ('self-cleaning'). That property now holds only when the streamer is correctly wired; while unwired, stray USDC on this contract is unreachable (no rescue function exists).
